newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian stocks seen rising more to dividend season.
newsitem.headline: Belgian stocks seen rising more to dividend season.

text.p: After seven consecutive sessions of gains Belgian shares are expected to push higher still as investors hold on to stock in anticipation of dividend payouts in May and June, dealers said.
"We'll go higher until the dividends are over," one dealer said. Others were optimistic too, provided bond yields remained relatively low and the dollar held up.

The Bel-20 index ended 12.60 points or 0.57 percent up on Wednesday at 2,209.03, after coming within 10 points of its intra-day high of 2,230.50 set on March 11. The index shed some gains after Wall Street opened weaker in the afternoon.
Volume was again boosted by Bel-20 basket buying from one large bank and an insurance company to cover index-linked derivative products they are launching, dealers said.
Among Bel-20 component stocks 17 ended higher, one unchanged and two - oil major Petrofina and insurer Royale Blege easier.

Retailer Colruyt, which some analysts like but consider expensive, climbed 1.58 percent to 14,425 francs and one dealer refered to Belgian newspaper reports that Colruyt had increased its market share in Belgium. Dollar sensitive rival Delhaize rose 1.39 percent to 1,820 francs.

Top loser in percentage terms was construction firm Franki, which fell 4.1 percent to 470 francs, though volume was low at 2,160 shares. The company announced late on Tuesday that its group loss narrowed in 1996, but said it would again not be paying a dividend this year.
